      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/kilder-til-nrk_-brenna-og-liland-skal-motes-1.18089667</link>
      <description>For å prøve å løse budsjettfloken på Stortinget er det kontakt mellom de parlamentariske lederne i Ap, MDG, SV, Rødt og Senterpartiet, etter det NRK erfarer.
Det er også planlagt direkte samtaler mellom Arbeiderpartiets Tonje Brenna og MDGs Ingrid Liland i dag.
Kilder i partiene sier lite tyder på en snarlig løsning, som kan få MDG om bord.
For Ap, SV, Sp og Rødt framstår det som uklart hva MDG forlanger av konkrete gjennomslag for å kunne stemme for statsbudsjettet.
De fire partiene har på sin side så langt avvist å endre budsjettavtalen som ble inngått onsdag.
Finanskomiteen på Stortinget skal avgi sin innstilling om statsbudsjett på mandag. Selve voteringen i stortingssalen skjer 7. desember.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Mann tok seg inn i boligen til Høiby – nå er saken henlagt</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/mann-tok-seg-inn-i-boligen-til-hoiby-_-na-er-saken-henlagt-1.18089585</link>
      <description>Politiet har etterforsket saken der en mann tok seg inn til Marius Borg Høiby på Skaugum og har besluttet å henlegge saken etter bevisets stilling.
Det opplyser Oslo politidistrikt i en pressemelding fredag.
– Påtalemyndigheten har kommet til at det etter etterforskningen er rimelig tvil om siktedes skyldevne på tidspunktet for den anmeldte hendelsen, skriver politiet.
Mannen har ikke ønsket å forklare seg for politiet, men det er gjennomført avhør av fornærmede og vitneavhør. Han har selv nektet for å ha gjort noe straffbart.
I tillegg er det gjennomført en primærpsykiatrisk undersøkelse av siktede og innhentet rapporter, ifølge politiet.
Det var ikke Høiby som anmeldte saken.
– Det var politiet som opprettet saken, og det har ingen betydning for oss at dette blir henlagt. Det viktigste for oss er at hans sikkerhet er ivaretatt, noe Høiby opplever at den er, sier Høibys forsvarer Alexander Greaker i en uttalelse til VG.</description>

      <title>Utbrudd av influensa: – Ta vaksinen nå</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/utbrudd-av-influensa_-_-ta-vaksinen-na-1.18089136</link>
      <description>Vinterens influensautbrudd er i gang. Samtidig øker koronasmitten.
Det opplyser Folkehelseinstituttet torsdag.
– Beskyttelse mot influensa og covid-19 oppnås én til to uker etter at du har tatt vaksine. Det er derfor viktig at de som er anbefalt vaksine tar den nå, før smitten øker ytterligere, sier overlege Ingvild Fjeldheim ved FHI.
Vaksine er det viktigste tiltaket for å beskytte risikogrupper og eldre mot alvorlig influensa- og koronasykdom, heter det.
Men forsinkelser i leveransene har ført til at enkelte kommuner har måttet vente med vaksineringen. Dette problemet skal imidlertid være løst nå.
– Har du måtte utsette vaksineringen fordi vaksinen ikke var tilgjengelig, oppfordrer vi deg til å ta vaksine nå, sier Fjeldheim.
Disse anbefales å ta influensavaksinen:
• Alle fra fylte 65 år.
• Barn og voksne i definerte risikogrupper.
• Gravide etter 12. svangerskapsuke, og tidligere i svangerskapet ved tilleggsrisiko.
• Helsepersonell med nær pasientkontakt.</description>
      <category>Influensa</category>
      <pubDate>Thu, 26 Nov 2026 12:14:16 GMT</pubDate>

    <item>
      <title>Nusa-dobbel for Leipzig i Meisterligaen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/nusa-dobbel-for-leipzig-i-meisterligaen-1.18088054</link>
      <description>Antonio Nusa briljerte med heile to scoringar for RB Leipzig i kampen mot franske Lens.
Nusa markerte seg allereie frå start og sørga for det andre av to mål for Leipzig i første omgang før det var gått ti minutt.
Etter pausen var franskmennene litt meir på ballen og fekk utteljing då Matthieu Udol plukka opp ein retur etter eit blokkert skot og sette ballen i mål.
Mot slutten sette Leipzig alle mann i angrep og Nusa fekk ein enkel jobb med å setta si andre scoring, få sekund før dommaren blåste av kampen.
Stillinga blei til slutt 3–1 til tyskarane, medan Lens held fram med skuffande resultat.
Den franske klubben vann den første kampen i Meisterligaen i haust, men har sidan gått på fire strake tap.
9. desember møter dei Bodø/Glimt på heimebane.
Martin Ødegaard og Arsenal spelte uavgjort mot Borussia Dortmund og Julian Ryerson.
Det same gjorde Manchester City som klarte å utlikna til 2–2 mot Napoli i det 86. speleminuttet, sjølv om Erling Braut Haaland var mållaus gjennom heile kampen.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Skandalen i Afrikamesterskapet: Senegal får tilbake tittelen</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/skandalen-i-afrikamesterskapet_-senegal-far-tilbake-tittelen-1.18087604</link>
      <description>Idrettens voldgiftsrett (CAS) har konkludert med at Senegal gjeninnsettes som vinnere av Afrikamesterskapet i fotball i 2025.
Det har Idrettens voldgiftsrett besluttet, ifølge nyhetskanalen Reuters.
Det er nesten ti måneder siden Senegal forlot banen i protest da vertsnasjon Marokko fikk straffespark på overtid i finalen. Kampen ble stoppet i nærmere et kvarter.
Marokkos Brahim Díaz bommet, og Senegal vant kampen 1-0 etter ekstraomganger.
Det afrikanske fotballforbundet (CAF) ga først ut bøter og utestengelser til Senegal.
I mars ble Senegal fratatt tittelen og Marokko tilkjent 3-0 og seier. Senegals fotballforbund anket saken til CAS.
I oktober ble det gjennomført en høring bak lukkede dører.
Tirsdag kom den endelige kjennelsen i tvisten.
Senegal møtte Norge i gruppespillet i VM i USA i sommer. Der vant Norge 3-2 etter en dramatisk avslutning.
(NTB)</description>

      <title>Ingen utsatt frist for de rødgrønne: Må avklare innen onsdag</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/ingen-utsatt-frist-for-de-rodgronne_-ma-avklare-innen-onsdag-1.18087741</link>
      <description>Finanskomiteen på Stortinget fastholder at fristen for å melde inn politiske forslag og omprioriteringer til statsbudsjettet utløper klokken 10 i morgen, onsdag.
Komiteen hadde et kort møte i dag klokken 13, der det ikke ble gjort endringer i fremdriftsplanen som gjelder for behandlingen av budsjettet på Stortinget.
I praksis betyr dette at budsjettforhandlingene på rødgrønn side må få en avklaring i løpet av dagen, kvelden eller natta. Dermed øker presset på de fem partiene som har forhandlet om statsbudsjettet siden 6. november.
En avklaring må ikke nødvendigvis innebære en budsjettavtale med et avklart flertall bak seg. I fjor la Ap, Rødt og Senterpartiet fram en avtale, som ikke hadde flertall. SV og MDG kom først om bord noen dager senere.</description>

      <description>To personer ble natt til mandag pågrepet av svensk politi i forbindelse med voldshendelsen i Alta søndag morgen, skriver politiet i loggen.
De to personene er bosatt et annet sted i Norge, siktet for drapsforsøk mot en mann bosatt i Alta.

    <item>
      <title>Mann siktet for drapsforsøk i Arendal</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/nyheter/mann-siktet-for-drapsforsok-i-arendal-1.18086690</link>
      <description>To menn er pågrepet etter en voldshendelse utenfor et utested i Arendal natt til søndag.
Politiet skriver at det var en uoversiktelig situasjon da de kom frem til stedet. Det var flere personer involvert i ulike slagsmål, ifølge politiet.
En av mennene som er pågrepet er siktet for drapsforsøk. Det er ikke kjent hva den andre mannen er siktet for.
– Fornærmede i saken er innlagt på sykehus med alvorlige kutt og stikkskader, men skal ikke være livstruende skadet, skriver politiet.</description>

      <title>Timon Haugan vant i Gurgl - McGrath kastet stavene i frustrasjon</title>
      <link>https://www.nrk.no/sport/timon-haugan-vant-i-gurgl---mcgrath-kastet-stavene-i-frustrasjon-1.18086663</link>
      <description>Timon Haugan leverte med presset som leder etter første omgang og kjørte inn til seier på slalåmen i Gurgl. Han ble med det første nordmann med verdenscupseier i Gurgl.
24 år gamle Eirik Hystad Solberg overrasket stort på og ble nummer to - hans første pallplass på toppnivå.
Atle Lie McGrath var nummer to før finaleomgangen, men hektet i en port og forsvant ut. I frustrasjon kastet han stavene og ble liggende ved siden av løypa. Også Henrik Kristoffersen, som var nummer seks etter første omgang, kjørte ut i finalen.
Lucas Pinheiro Braathen jaktet sin tredje strake seier - men 26-åringen kjørte ut i første omgang.</description>

A scenic destination on Vancouver Island was named one of the top “27 Best Places to Go in 2027” by travel magazine Condé Nast Traveler.

Clayoquot Sound, located north of Tofino, was ranked one of the top places to visit next year, and was the only location in Canada to make the list.

“Clayoquot Sound has long drawn adventurous travelers to Vancouver Island’s wild western edge—a maze of forested islands, secluded inlets, and old-growth rainforests,” said Condé Nast Traveler. “But now, Indigenous-owned hospitality is giving this remote luxury escape a deeper sense of place, shaped by the First Nations that have stewarded its lands and waters for generations.”

The travel magazine points to the luxury Clayoquot Wilderness Lodge as a popular accommodation, including among celebrities, as well as the new Wahous Wilderness Lodge, which is owned and operated by the Ahousaht First Nation.

“Guests are welcomed into Ahousaht territory with tide-to-table dining, a shoreline spa, and a ceremonial welcome in the cedar longhouse,” said Condé Nast Traveler.

RELATED: ‘To be self-sufficient’: Ahousaht opens luxury floating resort near Tofino

Besides accommodations, the travel magazine highlighted that Clayoquot Sound is a UNESCO-designated biosphere region, and says it showcases some of the best wilderness and wildlife – like orcas, humpbacks and otters – that Canada has to offer.

“New experiences and places to stay aside, Clayoquot Sound remains remote enough to preserve its deep sense of seclusion,” said Condé Nast. “This vast coastal labyrinth is best explored by water and on foot: Paddle between forested islands, walk beneath ancient cedars on Meares Island, hike Flores Island’s remote Wildside Trail, or soak in the geothermal pools at Hot Springs Cove.”

Condé Nast Traveler’s list of the “27 Best Places to Go in 2027” was created based on research and selections by magazine staff, travel specialists and editors.

Among the other selections are familiar destinations like San Diego, U.S. and Dartmoor, U.K. – to more exotic locales like the Albanian Alps, Zanzibar, and Jamaica’s South Coast.

The full list can be found on the Condé Nast Traveler website.

]]> 1364497 Victoria transit strike called off: Buses to run as scheduled Friday https://cheknews.ca/victoria-transit-strike-called-off-buses-to-run-as-scheduled-friday-1364759/ Fri, 27 Nov 2026 03:10:23 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364759

]]>

Public transit riders in Greater Victoria will be able to ride the bus as usual Friday, after BC Transit and Unifor Local 333 reached a tentative agreement during mediation Thursday.

The tentative deal calls off the one-day strike planned for Friday, returning service to Greater Victoria as scheduled.

“No picket lines will be set up, and fixed-route service in Victoria will operate as scheduled on November 27,” said BC Transit in a release Thursday, adding that “the BC Transit head office will remain open.”

Unifor Local 333, representing 729 transit operators and maintenance employees in the Greater Victoria Regional Transit System, is also ending both the overtime and uniform bans, effective Nov. 27.

In an email to CHEK, Stephen Bains, Unifor Local 333-BC president says “Our Members’ resolve shows that we are a strong labour union with deep roots in public transportation advocacy. Our members stood in solidarity with our riders and that is what got BC Transit back to the table today.”

“The workers and riders of Victoria can rest easy knowing that a good deal is on the table that will allow us to keep this region moving well into the future,” adds Bains.

Both parties say the details of the agreement will not be released until the deal is ratified, which is expected to happen in the coming weeks.

“Our organization understands the serious impact this job action, and the associated uncertainty, has had on our customers. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and are pleased that this tentative agreement has been reached.” states BC Transit.

The collective agreement expired on March 31, 2025.

The union announced the one-day strike on Nov. 20 after Unifor Local 333 said BC Transit had refused binding arbitration to settle the labour dispute. Members have been without a contract for more than 19 months, according to the union.

Two emergency responders on central Vancouver island are calling for drivers to slow down on Highway 19.

The Deep Bay Fire Department says it’s been called to multiple crashes this week and in one case, crews experienced a close call with one of their own vehicles. It comes as RCMP warn that drivers on that stretch of highway are simply going too fast.

On Highway 19 north of the Cook Creek exit there is a sign warning of hydroplaning. Despite the safety warning, the Deep Bay Fire Department has seen its share of crashes in this area during this week’s storms.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Between Monday and Wednesday it responded to four crashes on Highway 19 near Rosewell Creek.

“It’s not normal to see that many accidents in that short period of time,” said Fire Chief George Lenz of the Deep Bay Volunteer Fire Department.

Lenz says all four crashes happened in the dark, within a close proximity geographically to each other and the drivers were going too fast before hydroplaning and losing control.

“They were pretty much all weather related. A lot of rain. A lot of water on the highway,” added Lenz.

Fortunately no one was seriously injured, despite one being a rollover. But there was a close call. While responding to one of the crashes two firefighters in a firetruck were nearly hit on the highway as they approached a turnaround to get to the other side.

“They were slowing down. There were lights and sirens of course. They were slowing down to make the turn and a semi-truck went by them and was inches away from the mirror on the truck. It scared the driver and the I-C (incident command officer) who was sitting in this seat,” said Lenz.

It prompted the fire chief to ask people on the department’s social media channels to be more careful.

“Slow down. Drive for the road conditions. I mean there are so many accidents that we see that can be avoided just by cautious driving,” said Lenz.

It’s a similar message from a different emergency responder farther south on the same highway.

“For us it’s an alarming issue and we think it’s a trend,” said Sgt. Michael McLaughlin with BC Highway Patrol.

On Monday BC Highway Patrol released the number of speeders it’s ticketed so far this year on Highway 19 between Lantzville and Nanoose Bay.

“Way too much speeding and dangerous driving more broadly so we’ve written more than 1,300 enforcement tickets in a fairly narrow area of 15 kilometers and over 260 excessive speeding impounds. That’s way too many and we’re asking people to slow down because it is causing issues that really hurt people or worse,” said McLaughlin.

Police are asking people to drive to the conditions, avoid their phones while driving, and be sober and well rested.

They say only smart decisions will make the highway safer.

]]> 1364708 Convicted child killer granted temporary release in Greater Victoria over Christmas https://cheknews.ca/kid-killer-granted-temporary-release-in-greater-victoria-over-christmas-1364614/ Fri, 27 Nov 2026 02:25:05 +0000 https://cheknews.ca/?p=1364614

]]>

Convicted child killer Shane Ertmoed will be granted a temporary release from a South Island prison over Christmas to attend cooking classes.

In 2002, Ertmoed was convicted of 10-year-old Heather Aspin’s sexual assault, kidnapping, and murder.

Aspin was riding her bike outside her father’s Cloverdale home on Oct. 1, 2000, when she disappeared. Her body was found three weeks later, over 40 kilometres away, dumped in Alouette Lake.

After being arrested, Ertmoed confessed to police that he’d lured Aspin to his home, tried to sexually assault her, then strangled her when she fought back.

When he was convicted, the judge noted Ertmoed had no remorse.

Several appeals of his sentence and conviction were either abandoned or dismissed.

Very afraid, very angry

Upon hearing the news that Ermtoed had been granted a 60-day unescorted absence from William Head Prison in Metchosin beginning Dec. 1 for cooking classes in the Greater Victoria area, Aspin’s mother is furious.

“I’m very afraid, I’m very angry,” said Jody Aspin, Heather Aspin’s mother.

“I am scared. I am so so scared for what he is going to do to another child. No one wants my life,” said Aspin. “Please be aware, please be safe.”

According to the Parole Board, in 2025 Ertmoed was diagnosed with paedophilic disorder.

As of June 2024 he was assessed as “average” risk for future sexual offending, relative to other sexual offenders.

“According to the psychologist, if you were to sexually re-offend, the victim would be a pre-pubescent or pubescent female. Serious harm could result if a victim were non-compliant,” the report reads.

And despite his case management team opposing this release and the board itself raising concerns about whether Ertmoed would tell the truth to his supervisors if he began struggling with his thoughts, the Parole Board noted Ertmoed has completed counselling, and started taking medication to reduce his sexual arousal in November 2025.

Ertmoed has successfully completed escorted temporary absences starting in 2021, to participate in counselling sessions.

Watch the story in the video below:

Loading the player...

Last year he was denied day parole.

During his sentence he has completed five sex offender programs.

“Through programming and counselling you have gained insight into your sexually deviant thoughts and behaviours,” reads the Parole Board report.

His accountability, motivation level and reingratiating potential are all rated “high.”

Parole Board required by law to apply the least restrictive option

Starting Dec. 1, Ertmoed will participate in a cooking program with a Red Seal chef, attend counselling sessions, attend group outings, and live in a community residential facility in Greater Victoria.

Ertmoed’s release comes with the conditions he not have unsupervised contact with underage females, not use a computer, cellphone, internet, or access pornography.

“The law requires the board to apply the least restrictive option consistent with the protection of society in the decision it makes. In this case, the Board concludes…that the plan is adequate to the task of protecting the community and that you will not pose an undue risk,” Ertmoed’s parole decision reads.

Calls for release laws to be strengthened

In Ottawa today during question period, Conservative MP Frank Caputo for Kamloops-Thompson-Nicola called on the government to strengthen the laws that govern releases like this.

“This is completely unjust in our justice system, will the Public Safety Justice Minister commit right here and right now to changing it?” said Caputo.

“This government has brought forward tougher laws, sold tougher sentences and stricter bail conditions,” responded Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada Patricia Lattanzio.

“I’m talking about parole, not bail,” responded Caputo. “It is such an insult that this government does not take this seriously.”

The Liberal government says conditional release legislature is under review.

No warning to Greater Victoria

The Parole Board isn’t required to notify police of temporary releases, and in this instance, Victoria Police say they learned of Ertmoed’s release from the media.

The post Labour group says Bill C-39 changes fail to protect workers’ right to strike appeared first on CHEK.

]]>

The Canadian Labour Congress says the modest amendments made to the Liberals’ landmark economic legislation fail to protect the right to strike.

The federal government’s proposed Bill C-39 includes sweeping changes to speed up project approvals across the country, along with adjustments to the Canada Labour Code that would affect strikes and lockouts in federally regulated industries.

Since C-39 was tabled in September, union leaders have been hammering the government over changes that would spell out the labour minister’s power to end work stoppages in designated sectors like ports and railways if the national interest is at stake.

A House of Commons committee struck to examine C-39 wrapped earlier this week and made a few adjustments to the Labour Code sections of the legislation.

One set of changes affects a new special mediator role proposed by the legislation. The amendments lay out a process to appoint the mediator and gives that individual powers to dictate the schedule for mediation between the parties.

Another change would require a post-mortem study in Parliament every time the minister uses the powers in the legislation to quash a strike. That would include a debate in the House of Commons over whether the intervention was justified.

Siobhan Vipond, executive vice-president at the Canadian Labour Congress, said in an interview Thursday that Ottawa already has the power to intervene when work stoppages put the national interest at risk — by tabling and passing back-to-work legislation.

Adding a retroactive analysis after a strike has been quashed does not protect the rights of workers on the picket line, she said.

“Afterthought has its place, but not instead of actually having rights,” Vipond said.

The consequences for bargaining in C-39 revolve around proposed amendments to Section 107 of the Labour Code. The federal government has used that section multiple times in recent years to end strikes affecting Canadian ports and railways and other federally regulated businesses like Canada Post.

Whether existing legislation already gives Ottawa that power is the question at the heart of multiple ongoing court challenges. The government argues C-39 doesn’t grant any additional powers and instead puts “guardrails” on the use of Section 107 by adding the national interest condition and the need to consider the special mediator’s report.

The Canadian Labour Congress proposed amendments that would have established that Section 107 cannot be used to scuttle a legal strike. The group proposed the creation of an independent panel that could recommend back-to-work legislation in the event of an “extraordinary national emergency.”

Jobs Minister Patty Hajdu has promised not to compromise the right to strike.

In a media statement sent to The Canadian Press on Thursday, Hajdu’s office said that proposed changes to the Labour Code are the product of hours of consultation with stakeholders over the spring and summer, in addition to more than 100 hours of witness testimony at the C-39 committee.

The Liberals held a majority of seats on that committee, giving them ultimate control over which amendments were adopted.

“Together, these changes will help build a modern, resilient, and fair labour relations system that supports good jobs, stable workplaces, and a stronger Canada,” the statement from Hajdu’s office says.

Derrick Hynes represents Canada’s major railways, ports and airlines and telcos as the CEO of Federally Regulated Employers — Transportation and Communications, or FETCO.

Hynes said Thursday that C-39 is a “strong step in the right direction” after high-profile work stoppages at rails, ports and airlines in recent years. Proponents of C-39 argue Canada must protect its critical supply chains from disruption, particularly as Ottawa works to secure new export markets and sell the country as a destination for foreign investment.

Hajdu told reporters Wednesday on Parliament Hill that she thought the special mediator’s value had been glossed over in the C-39 debate. The mediator is automatically engaged in situations where negotiations have broken down in the past, and works proactively to bring parties together between bargaining periods.

Hynes agreed that public pressure from a special mediator could help keep parties at the bargaining table and reduce the frequency of government intervention.

But he said he would like to see C-39’s proposed changes go further by giving the minister the power to head off a strike entirely in the rare instances when the economic stakes are high enough.

“If there’s a special mediator’s report that indicates … meaningful collective bargaining appears unlikely in this situation, we believe it’s perfectly reasonable in those situations for the minister to intervene in a pre-emptive manner before a catastrophic work stoppage is allowed to occur,” he said.

Vipond said she doesn’t believe that curtailing strikes can benefit the economy. She said Canada’s economy is healthiest when its workers have a seat at the table.

The Canadian Labour Congress met with MPs across party lines in recent weeks to make their case on Bill C-39. Vipond said the vast majority of those MPs were receptive to the group’s concerns but are ultimately falling along party lines.

Opposition parties have largely said they’ll vote against C-39, but the Liberals are expected to use their majority in the House of Commons to pass the proposed legislation through third reading. The bill would then proceed to the Senate for another round of scrutiny and possible amendments.

Vipond criticized the rapid pace of the House committee study, saying it failed to give MPs and staff enough time to process the labour community’s concerns. The labour congress will continue its outreach with senators in a bid to get its amendments adopted, but she expressed similar concerns about a possible time crunch in the Red Chamber.

This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 26, 2026.

Defence Minister David McGuinty says he has been working to resolve a situation involving a government contractor and a nurse after Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre said her job was threatened over a photo with him at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright last month.

“I happen to agree with Mr. Poilievre that constituents should always feel free and MPs should always be able to speak to their constituents,” McGuinty said when asked about the matter at a House of Commons committee on Thursday.

Poilievre rose on a point of privilege in the House of Commons Wednesday. He said his privilege as a member of Parliament was breached when a nurse was told she might lose her job after she was photographed speaking with him in the aftermath of the tragic fire at the Wainwright base.

Poilievre’s Alberta riding includes Wainwright, about two hours southeast of Edmonton. He spent several days in the area after a fire suddenly overtook a training area on the base on Oct. 17, killing five soldiers and injuring dozens of others.

Poilievre said he met with the nurse, Maureen Carpenter, who works at both the Wainwright hospital and on contract with Calian Health. He said she talked to him about her experiences after the fire, when she helped triage and treat badly burned patients.

Thirty-nine people were injured in the fire, 19 of them critically.

Poilievre told the House on Wednesday that the “implicit message was that her contract would no longer have any chance of renewal, something that she had taken for granted before that point.

“Other work opportunities which were also expected to follow have since vanished.

“Simply put, it appears she is losing her chance to continue her work at CFB Wainwright because she met with her local MP.”

Poilievre said the situation affects his ability to do his job.

“If the people cannot speak to us, we cannot speak for them,” he said. “By threatening and imposing consequences on Maureen for speaking with me, the government’s contractor Calian is effectively interfering with my duties as member of Parliament for Battle River—Crowfoot.”

Poilievre said he contacted McGuinty after hearing about the situation but “the problems have only gotten worse” since then.

Speaking at the House of Commons national defence committee Thursday, McGuinty said he spoke to Poilievre about three hours after the Opposition leader had his conversation with Carpenter. He said the government has since looked into the issue and he has provided Poilievre with an update.

McGuinty said he has not spoken to Carpenter. He said that as a third-party to the contract, he has no legal standing to address it but he has spoken twice to Carpenter’s brother, including last weekend.

He also said he asked his deputy minister to raise the issue with Calian.

“I’ve been on this file, on this issue, because I’m very concerned,” said McGuinty. “It’s not right that a member of Parliament should not be able to speak to a constituent. And I don’t know any more detail than that. I don’t know what’s going on inside the company, but I’m hoping this can come to a successful outcome.”

The Canadian Press has reached out to Calian Health for comment but has yet to receive a response.

Kevin Lamoureux, Liberal MP and parliamentary secretary to the leader of the government in the House of Commons, said Wednesday the government has been and will continue to be there for members of the Canadian Armed Forces.

“I find it very upsetting to hear the comments with regards to Maureen,” he said. “We recognize the sacrifices and the emotions and the service that was provided by health care professionals, by first responders.

“I appreciate the member raising it, and I will report back, Mr. Speaker, once we’ve had the opportunity to look a little bit deeper into the situation.”

Deputy Speaker Tom Kmiec, who was presiding over the House Wednesday as Poilievre made his point of privilege, said Speaker Francis Scarpaleggia would return to make a complete ruling.

Bloc Québécois MP Gabriel Ste-Marie said his party would also look into the issue and get back to the House “soon.”
